title: Roundabout Crosswalks Are Set Back One Car Length From Yield Line: Yield to Walkers on BOTH Entry AND Exit!

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Both sedans face the same direction toward the central island, not head-on toward each other in one lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No car interior or steering wheel is visible; only exterior rear views.

single_bulb_signal.note: No traffic signal appears in the scene.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Same approach leg shows both left silver sedan and right blue sedan with fronts pointed inward toward the circle, so the right-side lane is driving toward the roundabout instead of away as a US exit lane must.

zero_text.note: All guide signs, yield sign, and license plates are blank geometric shapes with no letters or numbers.

scene_match.note: Shows a walker on a crosswalk with two yielding sedans, but fails to show BOTH entry AND exit behavior: both cars point inward toward the circle instead of one entering and one exiting away.

result.summary: Exit-direction geometry is reversed with both cars facing the roundabout, violating US right-hand traffic and teaching wrong exit behavior, so reject.

teaching_correct.note: Teaches wrong-way exit: the blue sedan on the right/exit side faces toward the circle instead of away, so a learner would think exiting traffic drives inward.

result.what_i_see: Sunset roundabout with central fountain island, a silver sedan on the left and a blue sedan on the right both stopped facing the circle at a striped crosswalk where a woman with backpack is walking.
